outcomes: Decides in an unlabeled position whether to remove an enemy obstruction or leave it, by counting attackers and defenders
Removes an obstruction with the cheaper man when the count allows
Tells when a pawn blocks no line of the opponent's rook, bishop or queen
sources: content/lessons/L-POS-OBSTRUCT-1.json; content/items/lesson-ds56.json (IBds56-20 to IBds56-22); shipped items IBp3-OBS-7

steps.text: In **Obstructions: name what blocks the line** you named what blocks each long-range piece. Now decide what to do with an enemy obstruction: **remove** it, **leave** it, or notice that it blocks nothing of yours. Count attackers against defenders first. If you remove it, choose the man that takes: the cheaper man usually goes first, but check the count.

*Rule of thumb:* remove the obstruction when your attackers outnumber its defenders and a cheap man can take; leave it when the count is level or the exchange costs more than it gains. It only troubles the side whose line it blocks. Your own blocked pawn is harder to remove: that is a paper exercise at the end, not checked by the app.

steps.title: Remove, or leave?
steps.prompt: Two different positions. In each, a pawn that blocks a rook's file can be taken. Predict whether taking it is best, or whether Black should leave it alone. Then check.

Paper exercise (not checked by the app): find one of your own pawns that blocks your own bishop or rook in a game of yours. Write down how it could be removed (exchanged, pushed, or protected so it can be exchanged) and what you would need first.
